changes.before: Describe a small feature, review an AI proposal, apply it, and check the result.
changes.after: Treat AI-written code as a proposed change. Read it and test the behavior you asked for.

before: An AI coding proposal is a proposed change you need to understand and verify. Describe the promised behavior with examples before reviewing it: who should get a discount, how much, and what happens for invalid input. A confident explanation is not proof that code satisfies those requirements. Read the changed lines, then check the behavior that matters.

Validation should happen before the calculation. Number.isFinite checks that price is an actual finite number; it rejects NaN, Infinity, and numeric text. price < 0 rejects a negative number, while 0 is valid. Membership must be the boolean true, not merely a truthy value. Nonempty strings such as 'false' are truthy in JavaScript, so if(isMember) alone can accidentally grant them a discount.

For the exercise, the discount is ten percent rather than this walkthrough's twenty percent. Ten percent of 80 is 8, so a member keeps 80 - 8 = 72, equivalent to 80 × 0.9. A nonmember keeps 80. Validate the price first, then choose the member calculation. isMember === true prevents a string from receiving the discount. Invalid negative, NaN, or Infinity prices return null.

Review meaningful cases: valid member, valid nonmember, zero, negative, non-finite value, and a truthy string posing as membership. Keep the earlier working code in History or Git so you can recover if the proposal breaks a promised behavior. Explain why each branch exists before accepting it. For real money, fractional representation and rounding rules also need explicit decisions; this small number exercise checks the supplied arithmetic rule.

Implement finalPrice with the supplied names and confirm all relevant checks. An AI that changes only the first example might still get the nonmember case wrong. Ask for a focused explanation or hint when a line is unclear, then inspect and test it yourself. If a new change causes a regression, restore the known working version while investigating instead of treating the AI's reassurance as evidence.
after: Before accepting a change, say what it must do. Our rule gives members a 10% discount and leaves other prices unchanged. Invalid prices return null.
A program can pass one example and still be wrong. Check both a member and a nonmember so a discount given to everyone is caught.
A valid price is a number at least zero, with a finite value. Number.isFinite rejects text, Infinity, and NaN. NaN means an invalid numeric result.
Multiplying by 0.9 keeps 90% of the price. isMember === true accepts only the boolean true. Text such as "false" must not earn a discount.
Test a member, a nonmember, zero, a negative number, Infinity, NaN, and text in place of a membership flag. Each case checks a different part of the rule.
Complete finalPrice using the same rule. Read every changed line and run the checks. Keep a saved working version so you can undo a bad change. An AI's confident explanation is not a test result.

before: Write finalPrice(price,isMember). Return null if price is negative, is not a number, or is NaN or Infinity.
Apply a ten-percent discount only when isMember is true; otherwise return the original price.
Test price 100 with and without membership, zero, -1, NaN, and Infinity.
If the tutor is connected, ask it to review your change.
Explain each condition in your own words.
Practice recovery by restoring an earlier saved version.
after: Reject prices that are not finite numbers or are below zero.
Apply the discount only when isMember === true.
Run the normal and invalid-input checks.
Explain the conditions and keep a saved working version.

before: A valid price must be finite and at least zero.
Check invalid input before applying any discount.
Use isMember to choose between price * 0.9 and price.
after: Choose price * 0.9 only for the boolean true.

before.question: An AI change passes one example. What should you do next?
choices: Review the changed code and check relevant edge cases
before.explanation: One example is limited evidence. Review what changed and test the behaviors the feature promises.

after.question: An AI change passes one example. What should happen next?
choices: Read the changes and test other important cases.
after.explanation: One success does not check the whole rule. Test the other promised behavior too.

changes.after: This lesson checks a small arithmetic rule. Real payment code also needs a defined way to represent and round money.

headings: Review and keep a way back

project.title: A reviewed AI change
project.task: Complete finalPrice(price,isMember). Return null for invalid or negative prices. Give a 10% discount only when isMember is exactly true. Review and test the result.
project.done_when: All checks pass, each condition can be explained, and a saved working version is available for recovery.
